BUILDING CONSTRUCTION — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: BUILDING CONSTRUCTION
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Internal Cooking Timer
   B. International Cricket Team
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. Input Cable Tester

2. When learning Site Organisation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Site Organisation.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Site Organisation.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Site Organisation.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Site Organisation.

3. When learning Orthographic Projection, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Orthographic Projection.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Orthographic Projection.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Orthographic Projection.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic Projection.

4. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   B. Remove all guards
   C. Work alone with eyes closed
   D. Run with the tool

5. When learning Domestic Water Supply, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Domestic Water Supply.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Domestic Water Supply.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Domestic Water Supply.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Domestic Water Supply.

6. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   D. Ignore burnt cables

7. When learning Windows, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Windows.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Windows.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Windows.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Windows.

8. When learning Scaffolding, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Scaffolding.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Scaffolding.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Scaffolding.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Scaffolding.

9. When learning Construction Hand Power Tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Construction Hand Power Tools.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Construction Hand Power Tools.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Construction Hand Power Tools.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Construction Hand Power Tools.

10. When learning Appropriate Technology in Building, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Appropriate Technology in Building.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Appropriate Technology in Building.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Appropriate Technology in Building.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Appropriate Technology in Building.

11. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Monitor
   C. Keyboard
   D. Speaker

12. When learning Roof Construction, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Roof Construction.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Roof Construction.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Roof Construction.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Roof Construction.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Appropriate Technology in Building and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Orthographic Projection and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Aided Drawing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Scaffolding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Information and Communication Technology

2. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Site Organisation.

3. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic Projection.

4. A — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

5. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Domestic Water Supply.

6. A — Never touch live wires with wet hands

7. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Windows.

8. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Scaffolding.

9. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Construction Hand Power Tools.

10. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Appropriate Technology in Building.

11. A — CPU

12. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Roof Construction.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Appropriate Technology in Building; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Orthographic Projection; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Computer Aided Drawing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Scaffolding; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
